module.description: Establish a deep understanding of DevOps philosophy before diving into tools and practices.

lesson.content: The Three Ways represent the values and philosophies from which DevOps patterns and practices derive. Understanding these principles is essential for cultural transformation.

topic.explanation: Focus on the overall performance of the system, not just a specific team or department. Optimize for global outcomes rather than local efficiencies that create bottlenecks elsewhere.

topic.topic-title: The Second Way: Amplify Feedback Loops
topic.explanation: Create shorter and amplified feedback loops to prevent problems from propagating downstream and to enable faster detection and correction of defects.

topic.topic-title: The Third Way: Culture of Continual Experimentation
topic.explanation: Foster a culture that supports taking risks and learning from failure, and understands that repetition and practice are prerequisites to mastery.

lab.objective: Map the current software delivery process to identify waste, bottlenecks, and improvement opportunities.

lesson.lesson-title: DORA Metrics and Measuring DevOps Performance
lesson.content: The DORA (DevOps Research and Assessment) metrics provide an evidence-based framework for measuring software delivery performance and organizational health.

metric.name: Deployment Frequency
metric.description: How often an organization successfully releases to production. Elite performers deploy on-demand, multiple times per day.
metric.measurement: Count of successful production deployments per time period.

metric.name: Lead Time for Changes
metric.description: Time from code commit to code running in production. Elite teams achieve less than one hour.
metric.measurement: Median time from first commit to production deployment.

metric.name: Mean Time to Restore
metric.description: How long it takes to restore service after an incident. Elite teams restore service in less than one hour.
metric.measurement: Median time from incident detection to full service restoration.

metric.name: Change Failure Rate
metric.description: Percentage of deployments that cause a production failure requiring remediation.
metric.measurement: Failed deployments divided by total deployments, expressed as percentage.

module.description: Deep dive into Kubernetes architecture, advanced workload patterns, and production hardening techniques.

lesson.content: Understanding the internals of Kubernetes is critical for diagnosing production issues and making informed architectural decisions.

topic.explanation: The control plane manages the state of the cluster. It consists of the API Server, etcd, Controller Manager, and Scheduler. Each component has distinct responsibilities and failure modes.
Each node runs the kubelet (responsible for pod lifecycle), kube-proxy (handles network rules), and a container runtime such as containerd or CRI-O.

lab.lab-title: Cluster Autopsy: Diagnosing Control Plane Failures
lab.objective: Practice diagnosing and recovering from simulated control plane component failures in a provided lab environment.

lesson.content: Proper resource requests and limits are foundational to cluster stability and fair resource allocation across teams and workloads.

important-concept.explanation: Resource requests define the minimum resources guaranteed to a container and are used by the scheduler for placement decisions. Limits define the maximum a container can consume and are enforced by the kubelet.

lesson.warning: Setting resource limits without appropriate requests can lead to unexpected pod evictions and OOM kills. Always set both requests and limits for production workloads.
